hazards.control: Enclosed transfer, dust collection, respirators in the sand area.

tabs.overview: Mesh names give the sieve range: 100 mesh is fine sand for far-field placement and lower bridging risk; 40/70 and 30/50 are coarser for near-wellbore conductivity. Fracture conductivity is propped width times pack permeability, and it falls with stress, crushing, embedment, and gel damage. Shale wells today pump mostly regional 100 mesh and 40/70 sand at high intensity; ceramics appear in deep, high-stress wells.
tabs.engineering: Tested per API RP 19C: sieve distribution, sphericity and roundness, acid solubility, crush at stress; conductivity from long-term conductivity tests.
tabs.safety: Respirable silica at every transfer point; enclosed systems, dust collection, and monitoring.
tabs.evidence: PetroWiki fracturing fluids and additives (S50), propping agents (S51), API RP 19C (S52), API Spec 5CT (S27), API Spec 10A (S28), field practice (S9).
tabs.failure_modes: Crushed fines that plug the pack, embedment in soft rock, proppant flowback into the wellbore.

name: Proppant: sand, resin-coated sand, ceramic
function: The sized granular material pumped into the fracture to hold it open: natural silica sand at low stress, resin-coated sand for strength and flowback control, intermediate strength ceramic and sintered bauxite at high closure stress.
